calculators.description_native: Suwenta ng iyong net take-home pay kada buwan o cutoff sa pamamagitan ng pagbawas ng SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG (HDMF) at BIR withholding tax ayon sa TRAIN Law (RA 10963).

inputs.name: gross_monthly_salary
inputs.label_native: Buwanang Sahod / Gross Monthly Salary (₱)

inputs.name: pay_frequency
inputs.label_native: Dalas ng Pagpapasahod / Pay Frequency

inputs.name: de_minimis_benefits
inputs.label_native: De Minimis & Non-Taxable Allowances (₱/month)

inputs.name: overtime_holiday_pay
inputs.label_native: Overtime & Holiday Pay (₱/month)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. STATUTORY MANDATORY DEDUCTIONS:
- SSS Contribution (2024-2025 Schedule under RA 11199): Total SSS rate is 14% of Monthly Salary Credit (MSC), split as 9.5% Employer (ER) and 4.5% Employee (EE). Minimum MSC is ₱4,000 (EE contribution = ₱180). Maximum regular MSC is ₱30,000 (EE contribution capped at ₱1,350). For MSC over ₱20,000, mandatory Workers' Investment and Savings Program (WISP) applies.
- PhilHealth Premium (RA 11223 Universal Health Care Act): Premium rate is 5.0% of Gross Basic Monthly Salary, shared 50/50 between ER and EE (EE share = 2.5%). Monthly floor is ₱10,000 basic salary (minimum EE premium = ₱250). Monthly ceiling is ₱100,000 basic salary (maximum EE premium = ₱2,500).
- Pag-IBIG Fund (HDMF Circular No. 460): EE contribution rate is 2% of basic monthly salary. Maximum mandatory monthly salary base is capped at ₱10,000, resulting in a maximum mandatory EE contribution of ₱200/month (matching ER ₱200/month).

2. BIR WITHHOLDING TAX (TRAIN Law - Republic Act 10963 Revised Tax Table):
- Taxable Monthly Income = Gross Monthly Salary + Overtime/Holiday Pay - Total EE Mandatory Statutory Contributions (SSS EE + PhilHealth EE + Pag-IBIG EE) - Non-taxable De Minimis.
- Monthly BIR Tax Brackets:
  * ₱0 to ₱20,833 (Annual ₱250,000): 0% Tax (Exempt).
  * ₱20,833.01 to ₱33,333: 15% of excess over ₱20,833.
  * ₱33,333.01 to ₱66,666: ₱1,875 + 20% of excess over ₱33,333.
  * ₱66,666.01 to ₱166,666: ₱8,541.67 + 25% of excess over ₱66,666.
  * ₱166,666.01 to ₱666,666: ₱33,541.67 + 30% of excess over ₱166,666.
  * Over ₱666,666: ₱183,541.67 + 35% of excess over ₱666,666.

3. NET TAKE-HOME PAY:
- Net Pay = Gross Monthly Salary + Overtime/Holiday Pay + De Minimis - SSS EE - PhilHealth EE - Pag-IBIG EE - BIR Withholding Tax.

calculators.description_native: Kwentahin ang iyong statutory 13th Month Pay, Separation Pay sa ilalim ng Labor Code (Article 298/299), at Retirement Pay sa ilalim ng RA 7641 kasama ang ₱90,000 tax exemption limit.

inputs.name: basic_monthly_salary
inputs.label_native: Batayang Buwanang Sahod / Basic Monthly Salary (₱)

inputs.name: months_worked_in_year
inputs.label_native: Bilang ng Buwang Naitrabaho sa Taon (1 - 12)

inputs.name: years_of_service
inputs.label_native: Kabuuang Taon sa Serbisyo / Years of Service

inputs.name: separation_reason
inputs.label_native: Dahilan ng Pag-alis / Reason for Separation

options.label_native: Redundancy / Pagpapadami ng Tauhan (1 Month Pay per year)
Retrenchment / Closure / Labor-saving Devices (0.5 Month Pay per year)
Sakit o Incurable Disease (0.5 Month Pay per year)
Retirement / Pagreretiro under RA 7641 (22.5 days per year)
Kusa o Resignation (0 Separation Pay unless in Contract/CBA)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. 13TH MONTH PAY (Presidential Decree No. 851):
- Formula: 13th Month Pay = (Basic Monthly Salary × Months Worked in Calendar Year) / 12.
- Tax Exemption Limit: Under Republic Act 10653, 13th Month Pay and other benefits (bonuses, 14th month, performance incentives) are TAX-EXEMPT up to ₱90,000. Any excess above ₱90,000 is added to regular taxable income subject to BIR withholding tax rates.

2. SEPARATION PAY (Labor Code of the Philippines, Articles 298 & 299):
- Redundancy & Installation of Labor-saving Devices: 1 Month Basic Salary for every year of service. A fraction of at least 6 months is counted as 1 full year. Minimum payout = 1 Month Salary.
- Retrenchment to prevent losses, Closure/Cessation of operations not due to serious financial losses, Incurable Disease: 0.5 Month Basic Salary for every year of service, or 1 Month Basic Salary, whichever is higher. A fraction of at least 6 months is counted as 1 full year.
- Resignation: ₱0 separation pay required by law, unless specified in Employment Contract or CBA.
- Taxability: Separation pay due to involuntary causes (redundancy, retrenchment, disease) is 100% EXEMPT from income tax (NIRC Sec 32B6b).

3. RETIREMENT PAY (Republic Act 7641 - Retirement Pay Law):
- Minimum Statutory Retirement Pay = 1/2 Month Basic Salary for every year of service (fraction of at least 6 months counted as 1 whole year).
- Statutory Definition of '1/2 Month Salary' under RA 7641: 15 days basic salary + 5 days Service Incentive Leave (SIL) + (1/12 of 13th Month Pay = 2.5 days salary) = 22.5 days basic daily salary per year of service.
- Daily Salary Formula = (Basic Monthly Salary × 12) / 261 days (or 313 days depending on company work schedule).
- Retirement Pay is 100% TAX-EXEMPT provided the retiree is at least 50 years old and has served at least 5 years with the employer.

options.label_native: Indibidwal / Capital Asset (6% Capital Gains Tax)
Kumpanya / Developer - Ordinary Asset (CWT 1.5% to 6% + 12% VAT)

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. TAX BASE DETERMINATION:
- Under NIRC Sec 24D, all real estate transfer taxes are computed based on the TAX BASE VALUE, defined as the HIGHEST among:
  a. Gross Selling Price (GSP)
  b. BIR Zonal Value
  c. LGU Fair Market Value (Assessed Value in Provincial/City Tax Declaration)
- Tax Base = MAX(Selling Price, BIR Zonal Value, LGU Fair Market Value).

2. CAPITAL GAINS TAX (CGT - Individual Capital Asset):
- CGT = Tax Base × 6%.
- Payable to the BIR (BIR Form 1706) within 30 calendar days from notarization of the Deed of Absolute Sale.

3. CREDITABLE WITHHOLDING TAX (CWT - Business/Developer Ordinary Asset):
- Applies if seller is habitually engaged in real estate business: 1.5% to 6% depending on selling price bracket. Plus 12% VAT if transaction value exceeds VAT exempt threshold (₱3,600,000).

4. DOCUMENTARY STAMP TAX (DST):
- DST = Tax Base × 1.5% (₱15 for every ₱1,000 or fractional part thereof).
- Payable to BIR (BIR Form 2000-OT) on or before 5th day of the month following notarization.

5. LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT (LGU) TRANSFER TAX:
- Metro Manila / Cities = Tax Base × 0.75%.
- Provinces = Tax Base × 0.50%.
- Payable to Local City/Provincial Treasurer prior to Title Transfer.

6. LAND REGISTRATION AUTHORITY (LRA) REGISTRATION FEES:
- Computed per LRA graduated fee schedule (approx. ₱8,000 to ₱15,000 base + 0.25% of Tax Base for higher values).

7. NOTARIAL & INCIDENTAL FEES:
- Customary Notarial Fee = 1.0% to 2.0% of Selling Price.
- Real Property Tax (RPT) clearance and Certified True Copies = approx. ₱1,000 - ₱3,000.

calculators.description_native: Isumpay at ihambing ang babayarang buwis sa BIR gamit ang 8% Flat Tax Rate kumpara sa Graduated Income Tax Rate (na may 40% OSD o Itemized Deductions + 3% Percentage Tax) para sa mga freelancers, VA, at sole proprietors.

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. 8% FLAT INCOME TAX RATE OPTION (Sec 24A2b of NIRC - TRAIN Law):
- Eligibility: Non-VAT registered self-employed individuals, freelancers, and sole proprietors whose annual gross sales/receipts do NOT exceed ₱3,000,000.
- Tax Base = Gross Receipts - ₱250,000 (Exempt Annual Allowance for pure self-employed/freelancers).
- 8% Flat Tax Payable = MAX(0, (Gross Receipts - ₱250,000) × 8%).
- Percentage Tax Exempt: Taxpayers opting for 8% flat rate are EXEMPT from the 3% Percentage Tax under Section 116.

2. GRADUATED INCOME TAX RATE OPTION (Sec 24A2a):
- Deductions:
  * 40% OSD Option: Taxable Income = Gross Receipts × 60%.
  * Itemized Deductions Option: Taxable Income = Gross Receipts - Actual Allowable Business Expenses.
- Graduated Tax Brackets:
  * ₱0 to ₱250,000: 0% Tax.
  * ₱250,001 to ₱400,000: 15% of excess over ₱250,000.
  * ₱400,001 to ₱800,000: ₱22,500 + 20% of excess over ₱400,000.
  * ₱800,001 to ₱2,000,000: ₱102,500 + 25% of excess over ₱800,000.
  * ₱2,000,001 to ₱8,000,000: ₱402,500 + 30% of excess over ₱2,000,000.
  * Over ₱8,000,000: ₱2,202,500 + 35% of excess over ₱8,000,000.
- Percentage Tax (Sec 116): Non-VAT taxpayers on Graduated Rate must ALSO pay 3% Percentage Tax on Gross Receipts (Gross Receipts × 3%) via BIR Form 2551Q.
- Total Tax (Graduated Option) = Graduated Income Tax + 3% Percentage Tax.

3. VAT REGISTRATION THRESHOLD:
- If Gross Receipts exceed ₱3,000,000, taxpayer MUST register for 12% VAT, cannot use the 8% flat rate, and must pay Graduated Income Tax + 12% Output VAT (minus Input VAT).

calculators.formula_explanation:
1. ESTATE TAX COMPUTATION (TRAIN Law - Republic Act 10963):
- Rate: Flat 6% on Net Taxable Estate.
- Statutory Deductions Allowed:
  a. Standard Deduction: ₱5,000,000 for Citizen/Resident Alien (₱500,000 for Non-Resident Alien). No receipts required.
  b. Family Home Deduction: Up to ₱10,000,000 (must be the decedent's actual family home). If conjugal property, 50% of family home is deducted first, then up to ₱10,000,000 deduction is applied.
  c. Claims against Estate & Unpaid Mortgages: Documented debts of decedent.
  d. Surviving Spouse Share: 50% of Net Conjugal Estate.
- Formula (Married Conjugal):
  * Net Conjugal Estate = Gross Conjugal Estate - Claims/Mortgages.
  * Spouse Share = Net Conjugal Estate / 2.
  * Net Taxable Estate = Net Conjugal Estate - Spouse Share + Exclusive Estate - Standard Deduction (₱5M) - Family Home Deduction (max ₱10M) - Exclusive Claims.
  * Estate Tax Due = MAX(0, Net Taxable Estate × 6%).
- Filing: BIR Form 1801 within 1 year from date of death.

2. DONOR'S TAX COMPUTATION (TRAIN Law - RA 10963):
- Rate: Flat 6% on Total Net Gifts exceeding ₱250,000 per calendar year.
- Statutory Exemption: Gifts up to ₱250,000 in a calendar year are 100% TAX-FREE regardless of donor-donee relationship.
- Formula: Net Taxable Gift = MAX(0, Total Gifts in Calendar Year - ₱250,000).
- Donor's Tax Due = Net Taxable Gift × 6%.
- Filing: BIR Form 1800 within 30 days from date gift was made.
